mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a kitchen remodel and a kitchen extension?

acceptedAnswer.text: A kitchen extension builds outward past the existing exterior walls of your home to add new square footage, whereas a standard kitchen remodel updates the cabinetry, appliances, and finishes within your current floor plan. A remodel reconfigures interior space, but an extension involves foundation work, new framing, roof tie-ins, and exterior wall modifications. The main tradeoff comes down to usable space versus project complexity. While a standard renovation avoids altering your home’s footprint, an extension allows you to add large islands, walk-in pantries, or dining space that your existing layout cannot physically accommodate.
acceptedAnswer.description: A kitchen remodel updates elements within your existing floor plan, while a kitchen extension builds outward to physically increase your home's square footage and footprint.
